sources.entry: URL shortening is the action of shortening a URL to make it substantially shorter and still direct to the required page. Before hosting one, please see disadvantages of URL shorteners.

summary.name: URL (Uniform Resource Locator)
summary.one_liner: A URL is a reference to a web resource that specifies its network location and the mechanism for retrieving it, as described in the Wikipedia article on the topic.
use_cases: understanding the parts of a web address
handling non-ASCII domain names and paths
summary.what_it_does: The page is a Wikipedia article describing the Uniform Resource Locator, a reference to a resource on the World Wide Web. It explains the generic URI syntax (scheme, authority, path, query, fragment) with examples and delimiter rules. It covers the history of URLs from RFC 1738 in 1994 and the later RFC 3986 generic syntax. It also describes internationalized URLs (IRIs, punycode domain names, percent-encoded UTF-8 paths) and protocol-relative URLs.
notable: Explains the five-component generic URI syntax with the delimiter rules for each part
Covers internationalized URLs, including punycode conversion of domain names and UTF-8 percent-encoding of paths
Traces the history from RFC 1738 (1994) and the Berners-Lee origins
Lists references to the relevant RFCs and the WHATWG URL specification
caveats: The page is an encyclopedia article, not a tool; it is listed in awesome-selfhosted only as a pointer under URL shorteners
Article content is informational and may not reflect the latest standard versions
